title: T2* mapping of the knee joint cartilage under mechanical load during alpine skiing: establishment and longitudinal assessment
summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate changes in the articular cartilage of the various parts of the knee joint as a result of stress during alpine skiing.
For this purpose, the participants will undergo an MRI-scan of both knee joints before, immediately after and in the morning after skiing.
The researchers also want to find out whether the cartilage reacts differently to the stress of alpine skiing at the beginning and the end of the season.

interventions.name:
The study population is made up of experienced alpine skiers of different age groups. 
6 people participated in the feasibility study and there will be around 20 participants in the longitudinal study starting in November 2026.
A control group is not planned.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-experienced alpine skiers
-written informed consent of the participants after enlightenment
Exclusion criteria:
-age <18 years
-complete or partial incapacitation
-previous operations on the knee joints, e.g. cruciate ligament reconstruction or partial meniscus resection
-pre-existing osteoarthritis/chondromalacia, focal osteochondral lesions of the knee joints
-malalignment of the leg axes or individual handicaps that prevent symmetrical bilateral leg loading
-implants, especially in the lower extremities (e.g. knee prosthesis, plate osteosynthesis, etc.)
-general (relative) contraindications to an MRI examination:
   +pacemaker, defibrillator
   +insulin pump, ferromagnetic intracranial clips
   +metal splitter in the eye or other life-threatening localizations
   +Cochlea-implants, pregnancy, permanent make-up
-unstable medical condition that interferes with the examination
-claustrophobia
